newsitem.title: UK: Reuters Training Editor George Short dies aged 58.
newsitem.headline: Reuters Training Editor George Short dies aged 58.

text.p: Reuters Training Editor George Short, who introduced hundreds of correspondents to the ethics and practice of news agency journalism, died suddenly at the weekend at the age of 58, the company said on Monday.
He was found dead in his bed on Sunday after an evening out at the newly-opened Globe Theatre in London on Saturday. The cause of death was not immediately known.
Reuters, a news and information agency, said in a statement that arrangements for the funeral and a memorial service would be announced later.

Short, an immensely popular figure in the company for his ready wit and scrupulous journalistic standards, joined Reuters in 1965 and worked as an editor and correspondent in London and New York before becoming Training Editor in 1981.

Short, from Devon in western England, drummed the disciplines of international journalism into a generation of new entrants into Reuters. He also trained hundreds of journalists from newspapers, agencies and broadcasters from around the world under the auspices of the non-profit Reuters Foundation trust.

"For scores of correspondents around the world and hundreds of others who attended his courses or worked alongside him, George will remain one of the most vivid and influential characters in the company," said David Rogers, Reuters Europe, Middle East and Africa Editor.
